tools.name: tailnet_acl_get
tools.description: Retrieves the current policy file for the given tailnet; this includes the ACL along with the rules and tests that have been defined. This method can return the policy file as JSON or HuJSON, depending on the Accept header. The response also includes an `ETag` header, which can be optionally included when [setting the policy file](#tag/policyfile/post/tailnet/{tailnet}/acl) to avoid missed updates. Learn more about [policy file ACL syntax](https://tailscale.com/docs/reference/syntax/policy-file). OAuth Scope: `policy_file:read`. Required: tailnet (default: -). Optional: Accept, details. Returns the AclGetResponse.

params.name: tailnet
params.description: The tailnet ID. Use '-' (the default) for the access token's own tailnet.

params.name: Accept
params.description: Response is encoded as JSON if `application/json` is requested, otherwise HuJSON will be returned.

params.name: details
params.description: Request a detailed description of the tailnet policy file by providing `details=true` in the URL query string. Supplying any other value for `details`, or not sending the param, is treated as sending `details=false`. If using this, do not supply an `Accept` parameter in the header. The response will contain a JSON object with the fields: - `acl`: a base64-encoded string representation of the huJSON format. - `warnings`: array of strings for syntactically valid but nonsensical entries. - `errors`: an array of strings for parsing failures.

tools.name: tailnet_acl_preview
tools.description: When given a user or IP port to match against, returns the tailnet policy rules that apply to that resource, without saving the policy file to the server. Required: tailnet (default: -), type, previewFor.

params.name: tailnet
params.description: The tailnet ID. Use '-' (the default) for the access token's own tailnet.

params.name: type
params.description: Specify for which type of resource (user or IP port) matching rules are to be fetched. Read about [previewing changes in the admin console](https://tailscale.com/docs/features/tailnet-policy-file/manage-tailnet-policies#preview-changes). OAuth Scope: `policy_file:read`.

params.name: previewFor
params.description: - If `type` is `user`, provide the email of a valid user with registered machines. - If `type` is `ipport`, provide an IP address + port: `10.0.0.1:80`. The supplied policy file is queried with this parameter to determine which rules match.

tools.name: tailnet_acl_set
tools.description: Sets the ACL for the given tailnet. HuJSON and JSON are both accepted inputs. An `If-Match` header can be set to avoid missed updates. On success, returns the updated ACL in JSON or HuJSON according to the `Accept` header. Otherwise, errors are returned for incorrectly defined ACLs, ACLs with failing tests on attempted updates, and mismatched `If-Match` header and `ETag`. Learn more about [policy file ACL syntax](https://tailscale.com/docs/reference/syntax/policy-file). OAuth Scope: `policy_file`. Required: tailnet (default: -). Optional: Accept, If-Match.

params.name: tailnet
params.description: The tailnet ID. Use '-' (the default) for the access token's own tailnet.

params.name: Accept
params.description: Response is encoded as JSON if `application/json` is requested, otherwise HuJSON will be returned.

params.name: If-Match
params.description: This is a safety mechanism to avoid overwriting other users' updates to the tailnet policy file. - Set the `If-Match` value to that of the `ETag` header returned in a `GET` request to `/api/v2/tailnet/{tailnet}/acl`. Tailscale compares the `ETag` value in your request to that of the current tailnet file and only replaces the file if there's a match. (A mismatch indicates that another update has been made to the file.) For example: `-H 'If-Match: 'e0b2816b418''`. - Alternately, set the `If-Match` value to `ts-default` to ensure that the policy file is replaced *only if the current policy file is still the untouched default created automatically* for each tailnet. For example: `-H 'If-Match: 'ts-default''`.

tools.name: tailnet_acl_validate
tools.description: This endpoint works in one of two modes, neither of which modifies your current tailnet policy file: - Run ACL tests: When the request body contains ACL tests as a JSON array, Tailscale runs ACL tests against the tailnet's current policy file. Learn more about [ACL tests](https://tailscale.com/docs/reference/syntax/policy-file#tests). - Validate a new policy file: When the request body is a JSON object, Tailscale interprets the body as a hypothetical new tailnet policy file with new ACLs, including any new rules and tests. It validates that the policy file is parsable and runs tests to validate the existing rules. In either case, this method does not modify the tailnet policy file in any way. OAuth Scope: `policy_file:read`. Required: tailnet (default: -). Returns array of AclValidateItem.

tools.name: tailnet_keys_create
tools.description: Creates a new [auth key](https://tailscale.com/docs/features/access-control/auth-keys), or [trust credential](https://tailscale.com/docs/reference/trust-credentials) in the specified tailnet. Trust credentials include [OAuth clients](https://tailscale.com/docs/features/oauth-clients) and [federated identities](https://tailscale.com/docs/features/workload-identity-federation). The key will be associated with the user who owns the API access token used to make this call, or, if the call is made with an access token derived from an OAuth client or federated identity, the key will be owned by the tailnet. Returns a JSON object with the generated key. The key should be recorded and kept safe and secure because it wields the capabilities or scopes specified in the request. The identity of the key is embedded in the key itself and can be used to perform operations on the key (e.g., revoking it or retrieving information about it). The full key can no longer be retrieved after the initial response. OAuth Scope: `auth_keys` grants access to create machine auth keys. OAuth Scope: `oauth_keys` grants access to create OAuth clients. OAuth Scope: `federated_keys` grants access to created federated identities. Required: tailnet (default: -). params.name: deviceId

params.name: approved

tools.name: tailnet_settings_get
tools.description: Retrieve the settings for a specific tailnet. OAuth Scope: `feature_settings:read` - required to view all settings except those governed by the below scopes. OAuth Scope: `logs:network:read` - required to view the `networkFlowLoggingOn` setting. OAuth Scope: `networking_settings:read` - required to view the `httpsCertificates` setting. OAuth Scope: `policy_file:read` - required to view the `aclsExternallyManagedOn` & `aclsExternalLink` settings. Required: tailnet (default: -). Returns the TailnetSettings.

params.name: tailnet
params.description: The tailnet ID. Use '-' (the default) for the access token's own tailnet.

tools.name: tailnet_settings_update
tools.description: Update the settings for a specific tailnet. OAuth Scope: `feature_settings` - required to update all settings except those governed by the below scopes. OAuth Scope: `logs:network` - required to update the `networkFlowLoggingOn` setting. OAuth Scope: `networking_settings` - required to update the `httpsCertificates` setting. OAuth Scope: `policy_file` - required to update the `aclsExternallyManagedOn` & `aclsExternalLink` settings. Required: tailnet (default: -). Optional: aclsExternalLink, aclsExternallyManagedOn, devicesApprovalOn (plus 8 more). Returns the updated TailnetSettings.

params.name: tailnet
params.description: The tailnet ID. Use '-' (the default) for the access token's own tailnet.

params.name: aclsExternalLink
params.description: Link to the external tailnet policy definition or management solution for this tailnet.

params.name: aclsExternallyManagedOn
params.description: Prevents users from editing policies in the admin console to avoid conflicts with external management workflows like GitOps or Terraform.

params.name: devicesApprovalOn
params.description: Whether [device approval](/docs/features/access-control/device-management/device-approval) is enabled for the tailnet.

params.name: devicesAutoUpdatesOn
params.description: Whether [auto updates](/docs/features/client/update#auto-updates) are enabled for devices that belong to this tailnet.

params.name: devicesKeyDurationDays
params.description: The [key expiry](/docs/features/access-control/key-expiry) duration for devices on this tailnet.

params.name: httpsEnabled
params.description: Whether provisioning of [HTTPS certificates](/docs/how-to/set-up-https-certificates) is enabled for this tailnet.

params.name: networkFlowLoggingOn
params.description: Whether [network flog logs](/docs/features/logging/network-flow-logs) are enabled for the tailnet.

params.name: postureIdentityCollectionOn
params.description: Whether [identity collection](/docs/features/access-control/device-management/how-to/manage-identity) is enabled for [device posture](/docs/features/device-posture) integrations for the tailnet.

params.name: regionalRoutingOn
params.description: Whether [regional routing](/docs/how-to/set-up-high-availability#regional-routing) is enabled for the tailnet.

params.name: usersApprovalOn
params.description: Whether [user approval](/docs/features/access-control/user-approval) is enabled for this tailnet.

params.name: usersRoleAllowedToJoinExternalTailnets
params.description: Which user roles are allowed to [join external tailnets](/docs/features/sharing/how-to/invite-any-user).

novel_features.name: Route approval that keeps other routes
novel_features.description: Approve a subnet route or exit node on one device without dropping the routes it already has.

novel_features.name: Route unapproval that keeps other routes
novel_features.description: Remove approval for one route or the exit-node pair while leaving every other approved route in place.

novel_features.name: Safe policy entry insert
novel_features.description: Append one nodeAttrs, grants, acls, or ssh entry to the policy file with comments preserved, a local backup, validation, a diff, and a concurrency check.

novel_features.name: Policy rollback
novel_features.description: Roll the policy file back to a local backup after validating it and showing the diff.

novel_features.name: Tailnet route board
novel_features.description: See approved, pending, and stale routes and exit-node state for every device in one table.

novel_features.name: Fleet key-expiry report
novel_features.description: List every device by days until its key expires and flag the ones inside a window.

novel_features.name: Machine share audit
novel_features.description: List every machine-share invite across the tailnet with who accepted it and which invites are still redeemable.

novel_features.name: Machine share revoke
novel_features.description: Revoke machine-share invites by ID or by device and acceptor, with a plan before any delete.

novel_features.name: Reachability preview
novel_features.description: Show which policy rules let a user reach a device and port, against the live policy or a candidate file.

novel_features.name: Device dossier
novel_features.description: Get one device's identity, routes, key expiry, shares, and recent changes in a single record.
